findings.evidence: Simple.lean:255-263 `@[expose] noncomputable def simpleRepHom ... app a := if h : a = i then ... else 0`; the only app lemma is Simple.lean:274-286.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem simpleRepHom_app_of_ne (h : a ≠ i) : (simpleRepHom hQ x hM).app a = 0` (proved by `dif_neg h`) and drop `@[expose]` from `simpleRepHom`.
findings.issue: `simpleRepHom` is `@[expose]`d but only characterized at the generator (`simpleRepHom_app_generator`). Nothing describes `(simpleRepHom hQ x hM).app a` for `a ≠ i`, so a consumer must unfold the `dite` — the body is exposed to cover a missing lemma. No in-repo consumer unfolds it: `exists_iso_simpleRep_of_simple` only uses `simpleRepHom_app_generator` and `IsZero.eq_of_src`.

findings.evidence: Subrepresentation.lean:183-185, 190-206, 115-118; grep of Simple.lean shows only `pathSpan`, `.toSubmodule`, `toSubmodule_eq_bot_or_eq_top`, `pathSpan_*_of_isAcyclic`, `mem_pathSpan_zero`, `pathSpan_zero_eq_pathSpan_one_of_ne` are used — no body unfolding.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem mem_pathImages {y} : y ∈ pathImages x n a ↔ ∃ p : Quiver.Path i a, n ≤ p.length ∧ M.map p x = y := Iff.rfl`, tag `toSubmodule_pathSpan` `@[simp]`, and remove `@[expose]` from `pathImages`, `pathSpan`, and `ι`.
findings.issue: `pathImages` is `@[expose]`d with no membership lemma, so every use of `toSubmodule_pathSpan` downstream has to unfold the set-builder definitionally (as this file's own proofs do with bare `rintro ⟨p, -, rfl⟩` at lines 218, 223, 231, 243). Same pattern for the `@[expose]` on `pathSpan` (line 190) and on `ι` (line 115): neither body is used outside this module — `ι_app_apply` and `toSubmodule_pathSpan` already cover them, and `Simple.lean` only ever rewrites with the named lemmas.

findings.evidence: Subrepresentation.lean:110-112 gives only `toQuiverRep_obj`; the `map` field at line 95 is `ModuleCat.ofHom ((M.map p).hom.restrict ...)` with no restatement.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem coe_toQuiverRep_map_apply (N : QuiverSubrep M) {a b : Q} (p : Quiver.Path a b) (x : N.toSubmodule a) : ((N.toQuiverRep.map p x : N.toSubmodule b) : M.obj b) = M.map p (x : M.obj a) := rfl`.
findings.issue: `toQuiverRep` gets an `obj` lemma but no `map` lemma. Nothing states how a path acts on the subrepresentation, so any consumer computing with `N.toQuiverRep` must unfold `LinearMap.restrict` through the exposed body. This is the characteristic elimination lemma for the definition.

findings.evidence: Subrepresentation.lean:73-78 defines the structure with only `toSubmodule`; lines 141, 154, 172-176 all quantify over vertices because `⊥`/`⊤` for `QuiverSubrep` do not exist.
findings.fix: Add `instance : PartialOrder (QuiverSubrep M)` (`N ≤ N' ↔ ∀ a, N.toSubmodule a ≤ N'.toSubmodule a`), `OrderBot`/`OrderTop` with `toSubmodule_bot`/`toSubmodule_top` simp lemmas, and restate the dichotomy as `N = ⊥ ∨ N = ⊤` (the vertexwise form follows via `ext`).
findings.issue: `QuiverSubrep` is a public bundled subobject type with no order structure: no `≤`, `⊥`, `⊤`. Consequently `ι_eq_zero_iff`, `isIso_ι_iff`, and the headline `toSubmodule_eq_bot_or_eq_top` are all forced into vertexwise `∀ a, ... = ⊥/⊤` form, and no consumer can state or reason about `N = ⊥ ∨ N = ⊤`, or about containment of subrepresentations — which the roadmap's downstream Layer 2/3 material (composition series, socle/radical filtrations) needs.

summary: The new public surface leans on `@[expose]` in place of characteristic lemmas: `simpleRepHom` has no lemma for its components away from `i`, `pathImages` has no membership lemma, and `toQuiverRep` has no lemma for the action of a path. `QuiverSubrep` also ships without `≤`/`⊥`/`⊤`, which is why its headline dichotomy has to be stated vertexwise.
